samples.summary: `exploreUi returns the journal the tool actually wrote` mocks away the only thing that writes the journal, so its journal assertion cannot fail
samples.evidence: The test stubs `createServerImpl: async () => ({})`, so `createUiServer` — the component that appends action entries to the `journal` array — never exists. The only journal assertion is `assert.ok(Array.isArray(out.journal))`, which is true for the freshly-created `[]` regardless of whether exploreUi wires the same array into the MCP server and returns it. The named behaviour ("returns the journal the tool actually wrote") is therefore untested: swapping `journal` for a different array before `return { out, journal: ... }` would still pass. Nothing else covers it — `runHunt`'s funnel tests stub `exploreImpl` wholesale and supply `FUNNEL_JOURNAL` directly. A fix would be a `createServerImpl` stub that pushes a sentinel entry into the passed `journal` and asserting it comes back.
searchedFor: checked runHunt funnel tests which inject exploreImpl

samples.summary: exploreUi's per-retry session/journal/budget reset is documented as a correctness property and has no test
samples.evidence: The comment in `exploreUi` states that sharing state across `withRetry` attempts "would be a correctness bug rather than waste" because a second attempt's `actionRefs: [0]` would resolve into the abandoned attempt's journal. Both tests that drive `exploreUi` inject `askImpl = { withRetry: (fn) => fn(), ... }`, i.e. a withRetry that never retries, so the closure is invoked exactly once and the reset path (`await live?.session.close()` at the top of the retried closure, fresh `journal`/`budget`/session) is never executed. A regression that hoisted the journal out of the closure would pass the suite.

samples.summary: runHunt's forwarding of `fault` to the explorer and to every replay is untested, which is the exact failure mode this PR exists to fix
samples.evidence: `runHunt` passes `fault` into `exploreImpl(...)`, into `runPlanImpl({actions}, {repoRoot, attempts:1, fault})` and into `replayUiCandidate(..., { fault, ... })`. `grep -n fault scripts/agent/hunt-ui.test.mjs` returns only line 446 (the renderUiReport seeded-banner test) — no funnel test passes `fault` or asserts the stubbed `exploreImpl`/`runPlanImpl` received it. samples.summary: replayUiCandidate's new `fault` pass-through is not asserted by any of its four dedicated tests
samples.evidence: `replayUiCandidate(actions, first, { repo, attempts, fault, runPlan })` forwards `fault` to `runPlan`. Since replay is the stage that must run under the same seeded fault as the original observation, silently dropping it here would make every seeded candidate fail to reproduce, with no test catching it.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. `scripts/agent/hunt-ui.test.mjs:548-575` ("exploreUi returns the journal the tool actually wrote") injects `createServerImpl: async () => ({})` (line 566), which replaces the only component that ever appends entries to the journal. In `scripts/agent/hunt-ui.mjs:298-334`, `journal` is created as `[]`, passed to `createServerImpl` (line 309-316), and returned as `live.journal` (line 334); writes come solely from the MCP tool the stub removes. No compensating coverage: `createServerImpl` is stubbed to `{}` at both usages (lines 541, 566); `hunt-ui-tool.test.mjs:181-192,266-273` tests `createUiTool` journal appends but constructs its own journal and never goes through `exploreUi`; and the `runHunt` funnel tests stub `exploreImpl` wholesale, supplying `FUNNEL_JOURNAL` directly (hunt-ui.test.mjs:658-663). Real and blocking under the test-adequacy rubric.

verdict.reason: The seeded-run ledger guard is real and genuinely untested. `if (fault) {...} else { writeFileSync(ledgerFile, serializeSeenLedger([...seen, ...ledgerAdds])) }` sits at hunt-ui.mjs:905-912 inside `async function cmdRun(args)` (hunt-ui.mjs:821), which is not exported — the module's export list contains only pure helpers plus `runHunt`. hunt-ui.test.mjs:7-22 imports fourteen symbols, none of them `cmdRun`, so the branch is unreachable from the test file. The reviewer's claim that 'ledger' does not appear in the test file is wrong (lines 693-715, 737-774, 803-810 mention it), but those tests all assert on `out.ledgerAdds` returned by `runHunt` — the population of deltas, not the write decision — and `runHunt` pushes to `ledgerAdds` unconditionally at lines 1108, 1152, 1162 with no `fault` gating, so the reviewer's core point stands. The only `fault` usage in the test file is line 446, inside the `renderUiReport` banner test (435-456), which asserts on markdown text, not on any file write. I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: repo-wide greps for `serializeSeenLedger`/`seen.json` (only hunt.mjs:1133, hunt-ui.mjs:911, and hunt-fingerprint.test.mjs:118-124 round-trip tests), `seeded|SEEDED|positive control` across all *.test.mjs (hits are only the report banner and fault-argv-forwarding plumbing at hunt-ui-probe.test.mjs:248 and hunt-ui-session.test.mjs:73), `NOT written|fabricat|suppress` across tests, verify-hunt-oracles.mjs (no ledger/seen.json/seededFault matches), and `hunt-ui` in .github/** and all package.json files (no matches — no CI positive-control check). Nothing anywhere spawns `hunt-ui.mjs run`. Major under the test-adequacy rubric: a behavior change whose stated purpose is preventing a fabricated defect from permanently suppressing a real one ships with no meaningful test.
